The VAEGAN model consists of an encoder, a decoder, and a discriminator, all built on multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs).
The encoder maps 200-dimensional airfoil coordinates into a 32-dimensional latent feature space.
The paper proposes three methods to generate new airfoils: interpolation, extrapolation, and sampling in the latent feature space.
Interpolation and extrapolation involve combining latent feature vectors from existing airfoils, while sampling generates latent vectors from a Gaussian distribution.
The paper combines the VAEGAN model with a genetic algorithm to optimize the generated airfoils towards desired aerodynamic properties, such as lift and drag coefficients.
The genetic algorithm operates on the latent feature space learned by the VAEGAN model to evolve airfoil designs that meet specific performance targets.
The paper evaluates the quality of the generated airfoils by analyzing the latent feature representations and the aerodynamic properties of the synthesized airfoils.
The data-driven VAEGAN approach can generate a wider variety of novel airfoil designs, some of which exhibit competitive or even better aerodynamic properties compared to the training data.
The paper uses the UIUC Airfoil Coordinates Database, which contains more than 1,600 2D airfoils, to train the VAEGAN model.
The airfoil coordinates in the database are preprocessed by interpolating the upper and lower boundaries and selecting 100 points along the x-axis to create 200-dimensional airfoil representations.
The VAEGAN model is trained using a combination of reconstruction loss, KL divergence loss, layer consistency loss, and GAN loss.
The paper demonstrates that the learned latent features encode essential shape information and that different geometry information is encoded in each dimension of the representation.

The synthesized airfoils from interpolation, extrapolation, and sampling in the latent feature space show great novelty and some possess competitive or even better aerodynamic properties compared to the training data.
The genetic algorithm is used to optimize the generated airfoils from the VAEGAN model towards desired aerodynamic properties, such as lift and drag coefficients.

The data-driven VAEGAN approach presented in the paper offers an efficient learning-based airfoil design framework that encodes and optimizes the airfoil on the latent domain and synthesizes promising airfoil candidates for required aerodynamic performance.
